basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A task instance is stateful and assignable; a task definition or template is reusable and stateless.
Separates the time an event happened from the time it was recorded.
Can be performed by people or by automated agents under the same state model.

may: Claim, start, complete or release a task assigned to its role.
mustNot: Act on a task that is only a proposal as if it were an order.
Mark a task complete without meeting its completion criteria.
Reassign a task to someone outside the permitted roles.
requiresHuman: Accepting outputs where acceptance criteria require judgement.
Escalations that change deadlines or priority set by someone else.

considerations: Task data shows how individual people work; using it for surveillance or ranking needs clear purpose and consent.
Automated performers must be identifiable, so people know when a machine did the work.
affectedParties: Requesters and beneficiaries of the work

owners.steward: The task owner (requester or process owner) owns the instance; assignees own their performance records.

items: A task has a performer role, a state, a due time and completion criteria.
Confused with a calendar appointment (time booking) and a work order (contractual authorization).
Duplicate execution when two performers claim one task.
Missed deadlines when escalations are not tracked.
